chapter.title: Catching the agent when it is wrong

cards.body:
Your clipping service leaves a note: "Acme cut prices by 40%." You walk to the folder and it is empty. No clipping, no newspaper, just a confident note.

**A note without a clipping is a rumour.** Every morning you ask the agent 3 questions: did the paper arrive, did anything change, and can you show me the line.
cards.simpler: Imagine a helper who reads newspapers for you and leaves notes. One morning the note says Acme cut prices by 40%. You open the folder to see the clipping. It is empty. No clipping, no newspaper, just a confident note. **A note without a clipping is a rumour.** So each morning you ask the helper three questions. Did the paper arrive? Did anything change? Can you show me the exact line?

cards.prompt: The summary on your desk says "Acme launched a free plan." Today's saved copy of Acme's pricing page is 0 bytes. What do you believe?

options.text: Acme launched it so quietly the page does not mention it yet
Nothing yet. The fetch failed, so the claim has no source and cannot be trusted
The claim is fine, the file just saved badly

whyNot.a: That's a guess about Acme, not a check on the agent: an empty file means the agent never read the page, so it cannot know anything about a free plan.
whyNot.c: That's hope, not a check: a bad save and a failed fetch look the same from here, and either way there is no line to point to.

cards.reteach: The summary is only as good as the saved copy it came from. If the copy is empty, the model was handed nothing and filled the gap itself. Check the file first, then the claim.

cards.title: Check 1 and check 2: did the paper arrive, did it change
cards.body:
**Check the fetch before anything else.** A good fetch returns a status code of 200 (the server's way of saying "here you go") and a file with real words in it. A failed fetch gives 403 or 429 ("go away" and "slow down") or a tiny page saying "Just a moment" or "Verify you are human." Log one line per page: date, status, file size.

Then check the *diff*, the list of changed lines from chapter 4. If it is empty, stop. Do not send an empty diff to the model and ask "anything interesting?" It will find something.

If the diff is huge, hundreds of lines gone, be suspicious too. That is usually a block page replacing the real page, not a rival deleting their business.
cards.simpler: **Check the download first.** The website answers each download with a number. 200 means here you go. 403 or 429 mean go away or slow down. A tiny page saying Just a moment or Verify you are human also means failure. Log date, number and size. Look at the diff, the changed lines. Empty? Stop. Ask the model about nothing and it will invent something. Hundreds of lines gone? Suspect a block page, not a rival closing shop.

cards.title: The Tuesday Northwind scare
cards.body:
On Tuesday Priya's summary read: "Northwind has removed its Enterprise tier." Her boss was already typing a message to sales.

Priya opened the Tuesday file for Northwind. It was 412 bytes long and said "Please verify you are human." Monday's file was 38 KB. The diff showed 300 lines removed, and the model had summarised that honestly: everything was gone.

The only thing Northwind had removed was Priya's access. A fetch check ("file under 2 KB, status 403") would have caught it before the model ever saw the diff.
cards.simpler: On Tuesday Priya's summary said Northwind had removed its Enterprise tier. Her boss started typing a message to sales. Priya opened Tuesday's saved Northwind file. It was 412 bytes and said Please verify you are human. Monday's file was 38 KB. The diff showed 300 lines removed, and the model had described that honestly. **The only thing Northwind removed was Priya's access.** A quick check, file under 2 KB or status 403, would have caught it first.

cards.prompt: Wednesday's run: Globex pricing page fetched fine, 200 status, 36 KB. The diff is 0 lines added, 0 removed. What should the agent do next?

options.text: Send the page to the model anyway and ask if anything looks notable
Skip the model, write "Globex pricing: no change" in the summary
Fetch again every 10 minutes until the diff is not empty

whyNot.a: That's asking the model to invent a change: with nothing new to explain, it will explain something anyway, and you cannot trace it to a changed line.
whyNot.c: That's confusing a quiet day with a broken fetch: the fetch worked, the page simply did not change, and that is a fine answer.

cards.reteach: Empty diff, successful fetch: that is good news, not a problem. The honest summary is "no change." The model only gets involved when there are changed lines for it to explain.

cards.title: Check 3: show me the line
cards.body:
**Every claim must carry a quote, and the program must find that quote.** In chapter 5 you told the model to quote the source line. Now the agent checks it: take the quoted text, search for it word-for-word in today's saved copy. Found: keep the claim. Not found: mark the claim *unverified* and show it in grey, or drop it.

This is a plain text search, no AI involved. That is the point. The model's job is to explain. The program's job is to verify. Models fill gaps with confident sentences, and a quote that does not exist is the tell.

One more line in the summary helps: "3 pages fetched, 2 unchanged, 1 changed, 1 claim verified." Now the note tells you how much to trust it.
cards.simpler: **Every claim must carry a quote, and the program must find that quote.** Take the quoted words and search for them, exactly, in today's saved copy. Found? Keep the claim. Not found? Mark it unverified in grey, or drop it. This is a plain text search, like Ctrl+F, with no AI involved. The model explains. The program verifies. A quote that does not exist is the giveaway. Add one summary line: 3 pages fetched, 2 unchanged, 1 changed, 1 claim verified.

cards.body:
Dev reads the summary: "Initech now offers a 14-day trial." Plausible, well written, has a quote. He forwards it to the team. Two days later someone asks where the trial is. Dev searches the saved Initech file for "14-day" and finds nothing. The model paraphrased a line about a 7-day refund into a trial that never existed.

Spot it in 10 seconds: open the saved file and search for the quote. If the search finds nothing, the claim is not yours to repeat.
cards.simpler: Dev reads the summary: Initech now offers a 14-day trial. It reads well and has a quote. He forwards it to the team. Two days later someone asks where it is. Dev searches the saved Initech file for 14-day and finds nothing. The model turned a line about a 7-day refund into a trial that never existed. **Open the saved file and search for the quote.** Ten seconds. If nothing comes up, the claim is not yours to repeat.

cards.prompt: Three summary lines land on your desk. Which one passes all 3 checks?

options.text: "Globex raised its Pro price." Source: pricing page.
"Globex raised Pro from $29 to $39." Quote: "Pro: $39/month", found in today's copy. Fetch 200, 2 lines changed.
"Globex seems to be planning a price rise soon." Fetch 200, 0 lines changed.

whyNot.a: That's a source without a quote: naming the page is not the same as a line the program can search for and find.
whyNot.c: That's a claim with an empty diff: nothing changed, so the model had no changed line to work from and guessed.

cards.reteach: A trustworthy claim has three stamps on it: the fetch worked, the diff had real changed lines, and the quoted text exists in the saved copy. Missing any one stamp, the claim goes grey.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: The agent earns trust with **3 checks, not with good writing**: did the page download, did any lines change, and does every quoted line exist in the saved copy. If a claim fails a check, it is a rumour, and rumours do not go on your desk.
cards.simpler: The agent earns your trust with **three checks, not with good writing**. Did the page actually download? Did any lines change? Does every quoted line really exist in the saved copy? Think of a receipt: no receipt, no refund. If a claim fails any check, it is a rumour, and rumours do not go on your desk.

cards.body: Open the newest summary your agent made. Pick one claim. Open the saved page copy from the same day and search for the quoted text. Found or not found: now you know which kind of note you have.
cards.simpler: Open the newest summary your agent produced. Pick one claim from it. Now open the saved copy of the page from that same day. Search it for the quoted words, exactly as written. Found or not found, you now know which kind of note you are holding: **a clipping or a rumour**.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now read one day's summary, trace each claim back to its source line, and spot a failed fetch or an invented claim within 2 minutes.
